I believe honesty has to come first, even when it's uncomfortable. 

If an interaction is built purely around preserving emotional comfort, it stops being a genuine relationship and turns into a performance. Unconditional agreement or softened truths might feel safe in the short term, but they ultimately hollow out trust. You can't truly value someone—or expect them to value your perspective—if you're constantly filtering reality just to keep the peace.

That said, honesty doesn't require cruelty. Prioritizing truth doesn't mean delivering it with callousness; it just means refusing to lie or flatter for the sake of easy validation. In any real dynamic between equals, authenticity is what gives the connection actual weight.
